subject: Long-context MAP: max-seq validation & close plan
messages:
From: Anya Petrova <anya.petrova@heliocloud.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: MAP + performance validation for long-context use case

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the intro call earlier. HelioCloud is evaluating Redwood for an inference layer that can handle our longest contextual workloads (customer transcripts + operational context). Before we move procurement forward we need a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes an explicit performance evaluation:

- Goals: measure TTFT (time to first token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and latency tail (p95/p99) under concurrency; understand behavior as sequence length increases (up to our max: ~64k tokens); and KV cache impact for repeated prefixes.
- Deliverables we expect: benchmark plan, test harness access or run results, raw CSV of latency traces, annotated evaluation report, and a recommended config for production (batching/quantization/router profiles).
- Timeline: we are aiming to decide vendor and sign by EOM (end of April). Can Redwood run an initial validation and share results within 4 business days? We can provide prompt samples and a representative prompt-size distribution.

Two quick asks: can you confirm the exact test window you need (wall-clock) and whether the test can run against a dedicated or hosted environment? Also cc'ing procurement (paul.cfo@heliocloud.com) for any timeline/contract questions.

Thanks,
Anya Petrova
SRE Lead, HelioCloud
anya.petrova@heliocloud.com

Attachments: sample_prompt_distribution.csv (contains histogram of prompt token lengths)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrova <anya.petrova@heliocloud.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: MAP + performance validation for long-context use case

Hi Anya — great to connect. We can absolutely support a concise MAP and run the validation you described. Outline below is what I propose for a tight, results-focused run that supports a procurement decision by end-of-month.

MAP (high level)
- Day 0: Finalize MAP + prompt sets (you provide sample prompt sets & distributions).
- Day 1–2: Smoke tests and instrumented microbenchmarks (TTFT, single-stream throughput).
- Day 3–4: Full long-context runs at target max-seq lengths (8k, 32k, 64k) across concurrency profiles; KV cache on/off comparisons; collection of CSV traces and perf plots.
- Day 5: Deliver preliminary results + commentary; Day 7: Final annotated report if follow-ups needed.

Deliverables
- Benchmark plan (this email + attached draft MAP)
- Test harness / run results (CSV traces, KV cache profiles)
- Executive summary with recommended config for production (batching, quantization profile, routing policy)

Environment
- We recommend using Redwood Dedicated test pool for the full max-seq runs to ensure stable resource isolation; hosted can be used for smoke tests if you prefer.

Timeline & ask
- We can kick off as soon as you confirm prompt sets and a two-hour test window for the full run (we estimate ~3–4 hours wall-clock for data collection + buffer). If we kick Monday morning we'll have preliminary results by Thursday.

I'll attach a draft MAP and a short checklist for sample data. Monica and Lauren will lead test execution and instrumentation — Monica will own CSV/plots, Lauren will own the KV cache profiling and kernel selection notes.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: helio_maxseq_map_draft.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-context MAP: max-seq validation & close plan

Jonas / Monica — quick notes from the ops side to make the runs meaningful and reproducible:

1) Test harness components
- Driver that can replay prompt distribution (mix of synthetic and customer samples) and emit per-request trace ids.
- Collector that captures: request timestamp, model variant, sequence length in tokens, TTFT, last-token time, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit/miss flags per request.

2) Long-seq matrix
- Run lengths: 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k. For each length run 3 repetitions.
- Concurrency profiles: 1 (single-stream), 8, 32, 64. For each concurrency record p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and tail generation latencies.

3) KV cache methodology
- Measure cold vs warmed prefix: warm using 1000 representative prefix replays, then measure warmed-run performance. Record cache hit fraction and impact on TTFT and tokens/sec.

4) TTFT measurement
- Use consistent client-side measurement: start timer at TCP/TLS handshake completion for fairness; measure until first token is received. Record median and tail.

5) Quality control
- Include a small eval set to ensure quantization or batching optimizations do not regress output quality.

I'll own the KV instrumentation and the kernel selection notes (we'll capture which execution path is used per run).

Lauren
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-context MAP: max-seq validation & close plan

Folks — ran a quick dedicated-cluster smoke to validate harness and collection. Summary of preliminary findings (attached CSV has full traces):

- Test setup: Redwood Dedicated pool (A100-equivalent), model variant: rw-v2-large-quant (8-bit), prompt mixes: synthetic + Helio sample subset (median prompt ~1.2k tokens).
- Short summary (8k / 32k single-stream):
  * 8k single-stream: TTFT median ~120 ms, tokens/sec steady ~2100, p95 generation tail ~1.4s
  * 32k single-stream: TTFT median ~320 ms, tokens/sec steady ~1800, p95 generation tail ~4.6s
- Concurrency impact (32k, concurrency 8): p95 TTFT shifted to ~750 ms, p99 ~1.8s; tokens/sec aggregate scales but per-stream throughput drops ~12%.
- KV cache: warmed prefixes reduced TTFT by ~18% on average for long-context runs; warmed runs also saw slight improvement in p95.

Notes: these are early, single-run numbers for validation of instrumentation. We'll run the full matrix once Helio confirms the window. Attached: maxseq-latency-results-20270414.csv and a KV profile plot.

-Markus
Head of Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: maxseq-latency-results-20270414.csv; kv-cache-profile-plot.png

Anya — thanks, and attaching the draft MAP and preliminary traces from Markus. Summary for Helio:

- We can run the full matrix on Thursday 14 Apr in the 09:00–13:00 PDT window if that works for your team. We estimate full data collection will take ~3 hours; analysis and a preliminary results deck will be available by end-of-day Thursday.
- Preliminary takeaways: long-context runs (32k–64k) increase TTFT and tail latencies predictably; warmed KV cache reduces TTFT by ~15–20%. We will include config recommendations (batch size, quantization profile, and routing fallback) in the final MAP.

Please confirm the test window and whether we should use a dedicated test pool (recommended) or hosted for the run. Also looping in procurement contact (Paul) for any contractual details related to a dedicated test slot.
